newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk banks brace for short-term bill auction - poll.
newsitem.headline: Turk banks brace for short-term bill auction - poll.

text.p: A poll of Turkish bankers on Thursday predicted that political worries would force the Treasury to set next week's bill auction with a maturity of less than one year.

The Treasury had been issuing only two-year, inflation-indexed bonds since April 1 as part of its drive to extend the maturity on its domestic borrowing after launching the new instrument at auction in March.

But seven of the 16 bankers polled estimated the maturity of the next auction to be set at nine months and two bankers at between nine and 12 months. Only one banker expects the treasury to hold an inflation-indexed two-year bond auction.

Bankers say recent political turmoil and increased uncertainties over the future of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist-led coalition government would weaken the treasury's ability to auction long-term bonds.
They say long-term paper may not gather enough demand from banks scared by the political crisis. The poll was carried out Reuters on May 27-28
The treasury is likely to issue new papers next week to finance its bond repayment of 288.2 trillion lira on June 4.
A banker predicted that the treasury may offer bonds to the public as an alternative way of raising money to match its bond redemption.
Another banker said the treasury may call for an inflation indexed bond auction and a six month t-bill auction at the same time.

Demand had remained low in the last two-year inflation-indexed bond auction on May 13 when the treasury sold 55.27 trillion lira worth of bonds at a risk premium of 29.95 percent, up sharply from 25 percent in the May 6 auction.
Last week it had also sold a nominal 40 trillion lira of 362-day bills to the public, out of an initial offer of 110 trillion lira.
